https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/07/25/w.text: Trump’s heavy hand in Colombia’s right-wing victory President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella, third from right, attends with his wife, Ana Lucía Pineda, Medellín Mayor Federico Gutiérrez, left, and Rodrigo Lara, the president-elect's pick for interior minister, right, during the Independence Day parade in Bogotá, Colombia, Monday, July 20, 2026. Miguel Angel Lopez/AP Photo/Miguel Angel Lopez BOGOTÁ, Colombia — First came President Trump’s “complete and total endorsement” of Abelardo De La Espriella, the right-wing candidate in Colombia’s presidential election. Then came the support of Republican members of Congress, who asserted that De La Espriella would have US interests in mind and helped mobilize Colombians abroad, who tend to lean conservative, to vote. Then, just days before the election, US immigration authorities detained an activist critical of De La Espriella and who had urged Colombians in the United States not to vote for him. The activist, according to a memo signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, had been interfering with US foreign policy. De La Espriella won Colombia’s presidential vote Sunday by a razor-thin margin — helped by ballots cast outside the country — and will take office in August. Experts say that even in an era when meddling in foreign elections has become increasingly common, the recent involvement of the Trump administration and its allies in Colombia’s election has been heavy-handed. The detention of an activist who opposed a candidate endorsed by Trump was particularly striking, experts said. “The attempt to quash dissent in a coordinated manner with the Trump administration, extending from Colombia to US soil — I can’t think of anything in recent times, in the 21st century, that resembles that,” said Alexander Main, the director of international policy at the Center for Economic and Policy Research in Washington. The State Department did not respond to requests for comment about the detention of the Colombian activist. Espriella, a lawyer who had never held office, energized millions of Colombian voters, and he appeared likely to win even before Trump’s endorsement. But in Colombia, President Gustavo Petro, a leftist and political opponent of De La Espriella, seized on Trump’s endorsement as he sought to sow doubt in the result, claiming that America’s involvement amounted to “cheating” that undermined the vote. This, in turn, set those in his inner circle rushing to stop the president from flat-out rejecting the result and calling for mass protests. The day after the election, Petro flew to Panama for an event but was in such a frenzy over De La Espriella’s minuscule lead over his party’s candidate — about 250,000 votes, or less than 1 percentage point — that his top ministers convened an emergency meeting in Bogotá, Colombia, to address what Petro believed were irregularities, according to two people with direct knowledge of the events who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss a sensitive matter. All the while, Petro kept sending messages to his millions of followers on the social platform X, and supporters streamed into the streets of the capital for a march called “Electoral Steal,” even as his party’s candidate, Iván Cepeda, counseled calm. On Wednesday, De La Espriella’s political opponent, Cepeda, conceded the election after electoral authorities completed a customary vote verification process. Since Sunday, scattered protests have broken out in Bogotá and the city of Cali, with reports of vandalism and isolated clashes with the police, but there have been no large demonstrations. The election pitted De La Espriella, a wealthy lawyer, against Cepeda, a senator, peace negotiator and stalwart of the left. De La Espriella used AI-generated images of a tiger as his campaign avatar and promised to “disembowel” political opponents, crush “narco-terrorists,” and strengthen ties to the United States. He lived in Florida for more than a decade and was recently naturalized as a US citizen. Esteban González Pons, the head of the European Union Electoral Observation Mission in Colombia, told reporters Tuesday in response to a question about Trump’s endorsement and the presence of US lawmakers in Colombia that claims of international interference were “absolutely irrelevant” to the election because “the Colombian people had voted freely.” On Election Day, two members of the U.S. Congress were in Colombia to stump for De La Espriella. Representative María Elvira Salazar, a Florida Republican, speaking in the city of Barranquilla, on Colombia’s Caribbean coast, told reporters, “We know very well that Cepeda will be Petro No. 2, so that’s why we’re with De La Espriella,” adding that a “profound closeness” with the United States was vital for Colombia’s prosperity. Senator Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican, who was born in Colombia and has emerged as De La Espriella’s biggest champion in Washington, also traveled to Barranquilla as an election monitor. He had raised alarms for weeks over Petro’s fraud allegations and supposed vote-buying by the left. The Republican lawmakers had spent weeks encouraging Colombians in the United States to vote, which analysts say helped tip the results in De La Espriella’s favor. In an election that saw a record-high turnout, the diaspora vote was, by most calculations, the decisive factor: De La Espriella received around 65 percent of the total overseas vote and around 80 percent in the United States. On Monday, Moreno, after meeting with De La Espriella, appeared to dangle a carrot: If Petro behaved for the next several weeks and did not interfere with the peaceful transfer of power, Moreno told a Colombian news outlet that it was “quite probable” that the US Treasury could remove him from a sanctions list. He was placed on the list last year after objecting to the Trump administration’s military strikes on boats it has said are carrying drugs. The administration has not publicly commented on the case of the progressive Colombian activist detained last week by US immigration authorities. In an interview with a prominent Colombian journalist Wednesday, the activist, Franklin Humberto Coral Garrido, better known as Beto Coral, said he had an open asylum case in the United States that gave him the legal right to remain in the country. Speaking from a detention center in Louisiana, Coral called his arrest “political persecution” and added, “My political activism focuses on Colombia, nothing related to the internal politics of the United States.” Coral was arrested by immigration authorities the same day Rubio signed a memo that said he could be deported from the United States. In the memo, a copy of which was obtained by The New York Times, Rubio noted that Coral arrived in the United States in 2015 on a tourist visa and had a pending asylum application. But “Coral Garrido has used his presence in the United States to conduct political activity in support of the Petro government” and has advocated against a candidate for president, Rubio wrote. The efforts by US officials and members of Congress to shape Colombia’s election have stirred outrage among rights groups and Democrats in Congress, who last week wrote a letter to top officials calling out what they said was “brazen interference.” It was once considered taboo for heads of state and other politicians to make public statements on foreign elections. Increasingly, though, such public intervention is becoming a regular part of global politics — on the right and the left — with Trump playing a major role in that trend. The US president has endorsed Viktor Orbán of Hungary and paid particular attention to elections in Latin America — supporting right-wing candidates in Honduras and Argentina. Presidents Javier Milei of Argentina and Daniel Noboa of Ecuador, both supporters of Trump, have also jumped in to endorse De La Espriella. Jennie Lincoln of the Carter Center, which monitors elections around the world, called this foreign involvement in the Colombian vote part of “an egregious trend of interference.” Lincoln is the head of a mission in Colombia to observe the vote, and she pointed out that the Organization of American States, a regional body, prohibits foreign interference in domestic affairs. Trump, who had repeatedly posted about De La Espriella on Truth Social, said Monday that he had spoken with him by phone to congratulate him. “He’s going to be a great president,” Trump told reporters at the White House, adding that the US relationship with Colombia would be “much better.” This article originally appeared in The New York Times .

https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/08/20/augu.text: Menü Kereső Gyásznapot rendeltek el Kijevben, Zelenszkij szerint ez volt az egyik legcinikusabb és legkiszámítottabb orosz támadás Külföld Bánáti Anna Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Augusztus 20-án éjszaka és kora reggel több órán át támadta drónokkal és ballisztikus rakétákkal Oroszország Kijevet és környékét, a legfrissebb információk szerint legalább 15-en meghaltak és több tucatnyian megsérültek a támadásban. A légiriadó és az első becsapódások éjfél után nem sokkal kezdődtek, és kisebb-nagyobb megszakításokkal késő délelőttig tartottak. Az orosz légicsapásban és a rakéták, drónok elhárítása közben lakóépületek és oktatási intézmények is megsérültek, megrongálódott egy gyerekkórház is: a kórház termeiben betörtek az ablakok, a területén több autó kigyulladt. Augusztus 21-ére gyásznapot rendeltek el az ukrán fővárosban. Az ukrán légierő nem közölt pontos számokat az éjszakai támadásról, csak annyit, hogy Oroszország éjszaka több tucat ballisztikus rakétát, robotrepülőgépet és hiperszonikus rakétát, illetve 168 drónt lőtt ki az országra. Egy nő sétál át felrobbant autók között a kutyájával a karjában 2026. augusztus 20-án Kijevben, miután Oroszország újabb nagyszabású rakéta- és dróntámadást intézett az ukrán főváros ellen – Fotó: Reuters / Stringer Valerij Zaluzsnij, az ukrán hadsereg volt főparancsnoka, jelenlegi londoni nagykövet arról posztolt az X-en , hogy egyre nő az orosz terror. A nagykövet felszólította Ukrajna nemzetközi partnereit, hogy ne csak szavakban, hanem konkrét tettekben is segítsék az országot. „Ismét civilek haltak meg, és tucatnyian megsebesültek. Fájdalom, veszteség és pusztítás” – írta a bejegyzésben. Az elmúlt hetekben Oroszország egyre nagyobb intenzitással támadja Kijevet ballisztikus rakétákkal, kihasználva, hogy Ukrajnának kritikusan kevés Patriot elfogórakétája maradt. A Patriotok jelentik az egyetlen hatékony védelmet a ballisztikus rakétatámadásokkal szemben, amiket Oroszország általában drónokkal és más rakétákkal együtt vet be. Volodimir Zelenszkij az elmúlt hetekben több alkalommal is úgy nyilatkozott, hogy a Patriotok hiánya emberéletekbe kerül. A mostani támadás után X-en az ukrán elnök arról írt magyar idő szerint délután fél 2-kor, hogy Kijevben és a Kijevi területen még mindig folynak a mentési munkálatok, több mint 600 mentő, katasztrófavédelmis és rendőr dolgozik fővárosban és két Kijev melletti településen, Brovariban és Boriszpilben. Az ukrán elnök szerint összesen 30 lakóépület, egy általános iskola, egy óvoda és a már említett gyerekkórház rongálódott meg. „Ez az orosz támadás volt az eddigi egyik legnagyobb, legcinikusabb és legkiszámítottabb” – írta a bejegyzésben. Zelenszkij szerint az ukrán légvédelem az összes orosz Kalibr rakétát lelőtte, a robotrepülők elfogási aránya 93 százalék volt, és a drónok „jelentős hányadát” is sikerült lelőniük az ukránoknak. „A legnagyobb fenyegetést a ballisztikus rakéták jelentik. Ez pedig teljes mértékben az Ukrajnának szánt Patriot rakéták szállításától, így országunk partnereitől függ. Nem lehet csendben és közömbösen nézni, tétlenül állni, miközben az oroszok ballisztikus rakétákkal tesznek tönkre életeket.” Fotó: Tetjana Dzafarova / AFP A támadás következtében csütörtök hajnalban újabb drón zuhant le Romániában , az ukrán határ közelében. A román védelmi minisztérium szerint senki nem sérült meg, és anyagi kár sem keletkezett. A történtek miatt két spanyol F-18-as vadászgépet és egy román katonai helikoptert is riasztottak. Oroszország a szomszédos országok légterében történt incidensekkel teszteli a NATO elszántságát, nyilatkozta csütörtökön Andrij Szibiha ukrán külügyminiszter. Szibiha szerint Oroszország megsértette Moldova és Románia légterét az éjszaka Ukrajna ellen irányuló támadásai során, az ukrán külügyminiszter szerint nem elszigetelt eseményekről van szó. „Ezek az események Oroszország szándékos és rendszeres terrortámadásainak részét képezik. Az agresszor egyre inkább próbára teszi a NATO és partnerei elszántságát, megsérti a szomszédos államok szuverenitását és szándékosan kiterjeszti a háború által jelentett kockázatokat messze Ukrajna határain túlra”. Ursula von der Leyen, az Európai Bizottság elnöke a román légtér megsértése után fokozódó eszkalációra figyelmeztetett, az EB-elnök szerint hibrid háború zajlik. „Uniónk alapvető küldetése a béke megőrzése, ma ez azt is jelenti, hogy képesnek kell lennünk a provokációk és az agresszió elhárítására.” Ukrajna éjszaka tovább folytatta az orosz olajfinomítók elleni támadássorozatát, az ukrán főparancsnokság információi szerint Tatárföldön és a Krasznodari határterületen mértek csapásokat. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Santos Maria Chilel Soto, who was killed in Delaware Photograph: Iglesia De Dios Fuente De Verdad Delaware View image in fullscreen Santos Maria Chilel Soto, who was killed in Delaware Photograph: Iglesia De Dios Fuente De Verdad Delaware Delaware Partner of woman killed by US hunter who allegedly mistook her for deer says death ‘no accident’ Walter Moorhead, arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, murdered Santos Maria Chilel Soto, partner alleges Ramon Antonio Vargas Fri 25 Sep 2026 14.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 14.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The partner of a Delaware woman who was shot dead by a hunter allegedly mistaking her for a deer has said the killing was “senseless” and the hunter had “no excuse”. “I have never seen a deer with only two legs,” Minivaldo Velásquez told the Delaware public news outlet WHYY in an interview published on Thursday about the death six days earlier of Santos Maria Chilel Soto. “It doesn’t make sense – no.” Velásquez’s comments came after authorities investigating the case arrested 74-year-old Walter Moorhead on suspicion of manslaughter, which Delaware defines as recklessness causing the death of another person. State police investigators had previously said Moorhead was hunting from a ground blind near the community of Ellendale at about 7.40pm when he thought he spotted a deer and fired his rifle. Yet it was actually Chilel Soto whom Moorhead shot at and struck, according to authorities. Velásquez told WHYY that he, Chilel Soto and two of her children were walking through a harvested cornfield at the time of the shooting after going to dinner as a family. “She had a yellow blouse, and I was wearing a blue T-shirt,” said Velásquez, who also said the shooting happened about an hour earlier – when it was presumably more visible – than the time listed by police. Velásquez reportedly told police he applied pressure to Chilel Soto’s gunshot wound – which was to her torso – and called emergency responders. She was then brought to an area hospital and pronounced dead there, state police said. Investigators said they jailed Moorhead after speaking with him and determining that he shot Chilel Soto, purportedly thinking she was a deer. Hunting deer with a rifle was not in season at the time of the shooting, according to Delaware’s laws . But WHYY, citing information from Delaware’s department of natural resources and environmental control, reported that the property where Chilel Soto was killed had a permit authorizing the harvest of antlerless deer there outside the normal season. Investigators booked Moorhead on counts of manslaughter, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, and reckless endangering. In Delaware , the first two of those counts are considered class B felonies, which can carry up to 25 years in prison. Moorhead – a resident of Salisbury, Maryland – posted a $43,000 bond to secure his release from custody pending the outcome of the case, state police said. Velásquez later told WHYY that Chilel Soto’s killer has “no excuse – the excuses are unacceptable and senseless”. “That was a cold-blooded murder,” Velásquez continued. “It was not an accident. It was 100% not an accident.” WHYY reported that Chilel Soto was a mother of five originally from Guatemala. The outlet reported being told by one of Chilel Soto’s sisters, Yolin, that sane people trying to hunt “should make sure it really is an animal before shooting – and what kind of animal”. Yolin Chilel Soto also suggested there may have been a component of “racism” to her sister’s killing, according to WHYY. “This person should receive psychological help before carrying a weapon – and not just at the beginning. They need it continually,” Yolin Chilel Soto reportedly said. Attempts to contact Moorhead for comment have not been successful. He waived a preliminary court hearing on Friday, the Delaware news station WDEL . WDEL also reported that dozens of people in support of Santos Maria Chilel Soto gathered outside and in the courthouse on Friday. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/gov.text: The Budapest Times Government to double child benefit from 2027 Starting from 2027, the government will also double the enhanced child benefit paid for children with chronic illnesses or severe disabilities, Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced in a Facebook post published on Monday. The prime minister wrote that approximately 134,000 children currently receive this enhanced child benefit. For each eligible child, the monthly amount will rise from 23,300 forints to 46,600 forints. This represents 279,600 forints more in annual support for families raising children with chronic illnesses or severe disabilities. The increase will also benefit 28,595 chronically ill or severely disabled adults who are entitled to child-rearing support in their own right, the prime minister explained, adding that their support will rise from 20,300 forints to 40,600 forints per month. For them, this means 243,600 forints more per year. In a video attached to the post, the prime minister said that for single parents raising a chronically ill or severely disabled child, the monthly amount will increase from 25,900 forints to 51,800 forints. This represents an additional 310,800 forints per year for each eligible child. According to the Prime Minister, the increase also extends to children living with foster parents, in children’s homes, and in other institutions defined by law, as well as to temporarily placed children and others entitled under separate regulations. In this category, the standard monthly amount will rise from 14,800 forints to 29,600 forints, representing an annual increase of 177,600 forints. For children with chronic illness or severe disability, the enhanced monthly amount of 46,600 forints will also apply from 2027. Péter Magyar recalled their announcement that, from 2027, they will double the standard child benefit, affecting 1.7 million children and one million families. Every amount will double without exception, including support for parents raising their children jointly or alone, he said. He drew attention to the fact that in Hungary the amount of child benefit has not been raised for 18 years, since 2008, and that it has since lost more than half of its purchasing power. According to his information, more than 363,000 families today receive child benefit for one child; in their case, the benefit will rise from 12,200 forints to 24,400 forints. Over a full year, this represents an additional 146,400 forints. Nearly 274,000 families receive child benefit for two children, and for them the benefit will increase from 13,300 forints to 26,600 forints per child. For two children, the total monthly amount comes to 53,200 forints, meaning 319,200 forints more per year. For families with three or more children — of which there are 120,000 — the government is raising the support from 16,000 forints to 32,000 forints per child. For three children, the monthly family allowance will thus be 96,000 forints, an annual surplus of 576,000 forints. For four children, the monthly amount will be 128,000 forints, representing an annual increase of 768,000 forints. An additional 32,000 forints per month is provided for every further child. Péter Magyar spoke separately about the fact that for single parents raising their children alone, the monthly support will rise from 13,700 forints to 27,400 forints. For two children in single-parent families, the amount per child will increase from 14,800 forints to 29,600 forints, and for three or more children, the sum will rise from 17,000 forints to 34,000 forints per child. “For this historic step, we are providing nearly 300 billion forints in additional resources in the 2027 budget,” said the Prime Minister.
